title: selftest-selection.v1 — which self-test modules a set of changes can affect, and why
description: The manifest `.engine/tools/selftest_select.py` emits and `selftest.py --changed-from` consumes. It records a decision, never a verdict: it says which test modules a change could affect, not whether anything passed. It is NEVER merge evidence — for any change that touches the Engine, the complete inventory still runs in CI against the exact submitted head, and that run alone gates the merge; for a DEPLOYED copy's change set outside everything the Engine owns, CI's project-only arm runs the validator alone and the inventory runs nowhere, a disclosed and acknowledged narrowing (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#883, #758). Three classifications exist: `focused`, where at least one test module was positively selected and each carries its own reason; `full`, where the complete inventory must run and `full_reason` says which condition forced it; and `project-only`, a focused selection whose every considered path was a deployed project's own, so the derived-artifact guard is the whole selection and the run record keeps that name. The partition is total by construction and has FOUR categories: a Python file under .engine/tools/ narrows the run; a registered derived-artifact output is exempt, neither narrowing nor forcing full, which is safe because each of those outputs has its own HARD drift check in the validator suite — the other registered validation command, which this selector never narrows (an earlier wording credited the guard's test modules instead, and that is false for three of the members, whose test modules only exercise synthetic trees); everything else falls to `full`; and, in a DEPLOYED copy only, a path the change classifier (change_classification.py) places outside every Engine corner, declared root file and the live ownership register is project-owned — recorded under `project_paths`, contributing no tests. The third category is the catch-all, so a kind of file the selector has never heard of runs everything rather than falling into a gap. An earlier version of this description claimed only two categories and was left standing when the guard forced the third, and then three when the deployed project-only case added the fourth — corrected each time rather than defended. Both reason vocabularies are CLOSED enums rather than free text, so a reader can match on them and a reviewer can check the sets are exhaustive; reviewers specifically rejected 'a non-empty string', which any single character satisfies. Serialization is canonical (sorted keys, two-space indent, trailing newline) so the same tree and the same changed set produce byte-identical bytes and a digest of them means something.

schema_version.description: Carried in the document itself so the copy embedded in a run record stays readable on its own — a later manifest version nested inside an earlier record must still identify itself.

classification.description: `focused` means a proper subset was selected and every entry in `selected` names why. `full` means the complete inventory must run. `project-only` means every considered path was a deployed project's own and the selection is the derived-artifact guard alone — a focused run by mechanism, named distinctly so the run record and the Build's evidence never present it as an ordinary narrowing. There is no documentation-only or empty-and-pass state: a run is focused or project-only only when something was positively selected, which is what makes an unexplained empty selection impossible rather than merely guarded against.

changed_from.description: The commit the comparison was made against, as the caller named it. Null when the selector ran with no base — which is itself a `full` outcome.

changed_paths.description: Every repo-relative path that differed, sorted and de-duplicated. Drawn from three sources because each misses what the others catch: the diff from the merge base (committed adds, edits, deletions, renames), the working-tree status (staged and unstaged edits), and the untracked-but-not-ignored list — without which a session's own brand-new test module would be invisible to the selector meant to run it.

full_reason.description: Why the complete inventory must run; null exactly when the classification is `focused`.

code.description: `git-unavailable`: a git command failed or its output could not be parsed. `no-changed-paths`: nothing differed, so there is no basis to narrow. `path-not-classifiable`: a changed path is not a Python file under .engine/tools/ — the catch-all that makes the partition total, and the reason nearly every prose or governed-data change runs everything. `deleted-or-renamed`: the import graph is built from the current tree and has no node for a file that is gone. `unparseable-python`: a tool will not parse, so its imports cannot be read. `dangling-import`: an in-repo import resolves to no file, so the graph would be incomplete. `unreached-tool`: a changed non-test tool that no test module reaches, directly or transitively. `selector-unavailable`: the selector itself could not run, which is NOT the same as git failing. `derived-guard-unreachable`: a generated map's generator has no test importing it, so the guard set is incomplete — and an incomplete guard is the silent miss the guard exists to prevent.

detail.description: One plain sentence naming the specific path or command, for a person reading the manifest. The `code` is what a machine matches on; this never carries meaning the code does not.

selected.description: The test modules to run, sorted by path, empty exactly when the classification is `full`. Every entry carries its own reason: the manifest's stated purpose is to answer 'why did this run these tests and not others', and a list without per-entry reasons does not answer it.

module.description: The dotted discovery name, so a packaged module (`memory.test_ledger`) matches what `unittest discover` produces from the tools root and the runner needs no second naming convention.

code.description: `changed-test-module`: the test module is itself among the changed files. `direct-import`: it imports a changed tool directly. `transitive-import`: it reaches a changed tool through a chain of imports. Breadth-first traversal means the first time a test is reached is by its shortest path, so the distinction between direct and transitive means what it says. `derived-artifact-guard`: always included, whatever the import graph says, because ANY change can stale one of the engine's generated maps and no import expresses that dependency.

exempt_paths.description: Changed paths that were seen and deliberately waived — category 2 of the partition, the engine's own generated outputs. Recorded because this manifest's job is explaining why a test is or is not selected, and without it a reader cannot tell a path that was considered and covered by the guard from one that was never looked at.

project_paths.description: Changed paths the change classifier called a deployed project's own — category 4 of the partition. They contribute no tests and are recorded for the same reason exempt paths are: a reader must be able to tell a path that was considered and waived from one never looked at. Always emitted; empty in the home repository, where every path is the Engine's.
